segments.title: Wyman Ham's origins
segments.summary: The interviewer asks where Wyman Ham was from; Manetta only knew him from the audience and says he may have had no home and used drugs.

segments.title: Origin of breaks; Louis Dumaine, Ned and name changes
segments.summary: A question about where breaks come from leads to garbled talk of a player who read music, trumpeter Louis Dumaine, a high-note player named Ned from Baton Rouge, and Coycault's changed name and Bill Johnson's nicknames.

segments.title: Charlie DeVore arrives; talk of the tape and recorder
segments.summary: Charlie DeVore arrives and is greeted while the recorder runs, with chatter about the room and the tape.

segments.title: Bill George, the Orpheum tour and Tony Jackson in Chicago
segments.summary: Manetta describes Bill George getting jobs and sending for Baquet for the Orpheum, then his 1913 Chicago visit hearing Tony Jackson at a State Street cabaret, with a garbled ASR loop in the middle.

segments.title: Tape noise and trills on an old blues
segments.summary: Garbled passage about trills and a few phrases of a blues tried a month earlier, buried in repeated ASR loops.

segments.title: Holler blues, parades and street dancing
segments.summary: They discuss the holler blues in parades, the crowd yelling at the break, and street dancing; the interviewer then asks about the coon shouters at Pete Lala's.
